Convex hull collider landed: add_convex_hull(world, x, y, z, points, scale) NIF takes a vertex cloud + scale, runs it through Rapier's ColliderBuilder.convex_hull, and spawns a dynamic rigid body. Interior points are discarded by the hull algorithm, so callers pass canonical vertex tables from RapierLab.Dice without pre-computing hulls.

Geometry: dodecahedron_vertices/0 (20), icosahedron_vertices/0 (12), pentagonal_trapezohedron_vertices/0 (12), plus face-up rules face_up_d20/1, face_up_d12/1, face_up_d10/1. Face-normal tables use the dual-polyhedron identity — d12↔d20 (both regular Platonic solids' faces = the other's vertices), pentagonal trapezohedron↔pentagonal antiprism — so there's no separate face-normal set to keep in sync with vertex changes.

Two mob_dev-side gaps surfaced during verification (both filed as MOB-254 with follow-up comment):

1. mob_dev's cross-compile step (MobDev.NativeBuild.classify_project_nif/2) only looks at project_root/native/<name>/Cargo.toml, so a plugin's Rust crate isn't findable in deps/. Worked around by symlinking rapier_lab/native/lab_physics -> mob_rapier/native/lab_physics.

2. On device, mob_dev's flat OTP bundle (otp/rapier_lab/ holds every dep's beams + .app files) doesn't register per-dep lib_dirs, so Application.app_dir(:mob_rapier) raises inside Rustler's on_load — the load happens but code:lib_dir(:mob_rapier) returns {:error, :bad_name}. Worked around in mob_rapier by making the Rustler otp_app configurable at compile time (Application.compile_env(:mob_rapier, :otp_app, :mob_rapier)); rapier_lab's config/config.exs points it at :rapier_lab so the lookup rides the host app's known-good path.

Also required: :mob_rapier added to rapier_lab's extra_applications, and application:load(mob_rapier) called from rapier_lab.erl step 5 before the Elixir MobApp module loads.
